question: Forecasters do the best they can, but sometimes they underestimate or overestimate the probability that a storm system will cause a tornado. We are interested in how these miscalculations might influence your trust in future forecasts. Again, imagine that it is a Saturday morning at 8:00 AM and you see this forecast: [rand_clim_format]. As the day progresses, imagine that you see some rain and lightning, but the storm does not produce a tornado with 25 miles of your residence. How would this influence your trust in future forecasts?
